{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Salad Recipes|Salad Recipes]] | [[Cookbook:Appetizers|Appetizers]] | [[Cookbook:California cuisine|California cuisine]]

'''Louis dressing''' is a salad dressing commonly used with [[Cookbook:Seafood|seafood]] salads, such as [[Cookbook:Crab Louis|Crab Louis]] and Shrimp Louis. It can also be used as a dip or sandwich spread, or many other uses. The dressing is creamy but has a little spicy kick. This is not the "traditional" recipe, but it is the easiest for untrained cooks to succeed at.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (235 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]]
*¼ cup (60 ml) cup mild [[Cookbook:Salsa|salsa]] with green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]]
*¼ cup (60 ml) [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 ml) [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
*1 ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (7 ml) [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|worcestershire sauce]]
*[[Cookbook:Hot Sauce|Hot sauce]] (e.g., Tabasco, Crystal), to taste

==Procedure==
#Combine all ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]], and process until smooth. The goal is to have a pink smooth sauce with little green flecks.
#Pour the sauce into a bowl, cover, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes prior to use.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* For the traditional recipe, replace the salsa and ketchup with ½ cup [[Cookbook:Red Chile Sauce|chile sauce]] (or store-bought chile sauce), and 3 tablespoons each of finely-minced [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]] and green [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chili peppers]]. Instead of using a blender, [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] the ingredients in a bowl.
* Keep refrigerated.
